title: Regional failover walkthrough and playbook rehearsal - 2026-09-15
content:
Attendees: Jordan Kim (owner), Maya Ortiz, Luca Bianchi, Ava Singh, Ethan Park, Sofia Martinez, oncall: rachel.tan

Purpose:
Run a hands-on walkthrough of the regional failover steps for Redwood's inference surface, identify gaps in the runbook, validate automation hooks, and collect action items for improving mean time to recovery (MTTR) and traffic redistribution correctness. This was explicitly framed as a rehearsal (no real outage simulated on prod).

High-level scenario we rehearsed:
- Trigger: Complete AZ-level network partition in us-west1 region causing >95% node unreachable across primary GPU pools.
- Objective: Shift 95% of latency-sensitive routed traffic to us-west2 (same continent) and 5% to us-east1 for overflow. Maintain SLO for p50 < 120ms for reserved customers and graceful degradation for hosted tier.

Pre-req checks (what we validated before starting):
- Inventory of running node pools and reserved capacity: pulled from fleet-api snapshot at 09:00 PDT.
  - us-west1: 320 usable GPUs (G5 + A100 mix), 48 reserved for Dedicated customers (soft pin)
  - us-west2: 280 usable GPUs, 40 reserved
  - us-east1: 400 usable GPUs, 60 reserved
  - eu-west1: 360 usable GPUs, 50 reserved
  - af-south1 (edge): 64 usable GPUs (burst only)
- Health of KV cache service and model variant registry: green
- DNS TTLs confirmed to be 30s for region routing keys used in experiments

Walkthrough steps performed:
1) Observability and detection
   - Verified alert : INF-FLEET-REGION-DEGRADED fired in staging telemetry when we toggled the health signal.
   - Confirmed playbook: escalate to infra-oncall after 2 alerts or 3 minutes sustained.

2) Smart routing policy activation (manual override)
   - Used 'routing-control' play to change policy for latency-sensitive route: set primary to us-west2, secondary to us-east1.
   - Observed ephemeral increase in tail latency for warming sessions (expected).

3) Capacity reallocation / preemption rules
   - Triggered preemption policy for non-dedicated burst jobs in us-west1: freed ~60 GPUs instantly (note: this was simulated via tx simulator).
   - Confirmed autoscaler did not scale up new nodes immediately due to quota guardrails. Need follow-up to allow emergency burst to cross quota for 15 minutes automatically.

4) Cache warmup and KV replay
   - Identified two hotspots where prefix cache miss ratio spiked: model retrieval for 'chat-v1-large' and embedding model 'embed-512-v2'.
   - Ran KV replay script to warm top-25 prompts; decreased initial token latency by ~40% in the controlled test.

5) Fallback model variants and quantization switches
   - Rolled traffic for heavy long-context inference to quantized variant q2 at the edge in us-west2. Observed minor drop in output token quality score (~0.7% measured against benchmark prompts) but latency improvement of ~18%.
   - Decision: acceptable for hosted tier but not for Dedicated customers without explicit opt-in.

What went well:
- Playbook steps are clear and ordered, observers can follow escalation path without ambiguity.
- Routing-control CLI performed under 10s for policy change (within expectations).
- KV replay tooling reliably re-queued warmups; script idempotent and safe for repeated runs.

Runbook gaps and discovered issues:
- Quota escalation: no automated temporary quota bump for urgent failover; requires manual GCP support ticket in current runbook. Risk: slow scaling when we need cross-region capacity allocation.
- DNS propagation assumption: 30s TTL is optimistic; some vendors cache beyond TTL. Need health-check-based routing fallback (we had to monitor for 90s before confirming full cutover).
- Dedicated customer routing: no automated policy to preserve their pinned capacity when we reroute; manual coordination required with account teams.
- Observability: regional SLO dashboard did not show per-model cache-hit impacts by default. We had to combine two dashboards.
- Simulation fidelity: tx simulator does not reproduce exact cold-start profile for some quantized kernels.

Data & metrics collected during the rehearsal (synthetic / controlled):
- Time to detect (from injected health signal to alert): 18s
- Time from alert to manual routing override: 4m12s (goal: <3m)
- Time for traffic stabilization to new region p50 latency delta: +22ms on average
- Cold-start rate for new backend workers after switch: 12% requests experienced initial KV miss
- Quality regression for q2 variant: 0.7% on benchmark prompt set (needs larger eval)

Action items (owner — due):
- AJ-01: Draft automated temporary quota escalation play and API: Luca Bianchi — due 2026-09-22
- AJ-02: Add per-model cache-hit panel to regional SLO dashboard and default quick-link in playbook: Maya Ortiz — due 2026-09-20
- AJ-03: Create Dedicated-customer routing policy extension to honor pinned capacity and pre-notify accounts when failover might change performance characteristics: Ava Singh — due 2026-09-24
- AJ-04: Update DNS guidance in the runbook to include vendor-specific caching notes and fallback to health-check routing: Jordan Kim — due 2026-09-18
- AJ-05: Improve tx simulator cold-start fidelity for quantized kernels (add kernel startup traces + sample logs): Ethan Park — due 2026-09-30
- AJ-06: Schedule a smaller follow-up drill focused only on KV warming strategies and measurement: Sofia Martinez — due 2026-09-21

Risk notes and mitigations suggested:
- Risk: Manual steps for quota and dedicated-customer handling increase MTTR. Mitigation: implement automated escalation and policy flags for dedicated routing within 3 sprints.
- Risk: Quality regressions for quantized fallbacks could surface in customer-facing SLAs. Mitigation: record per-customer canary tests when toggling quantized variants and allow per-customer opt-out toggles.

Decisions made in this rehearsal:
- Keep DNS TTL at 30s but add explicit health-check based routing fallback after 45s of partial propagation evidence.
- Allow temporary quota bump automation for emergency up to 15% capacity for 20 minutes, controlled via internal playbook token.
- Do not auto-switch Dedicated customers to quantized variants; require explicit account opt-in and notification.

Follow-up schedule:
- Quick sync on AJ-02 and AJ-04 next Monday 2026-09-20 09:30 PDT (15m).
- Full red-team style rehearsal (injecting multi-region faults) planned for 2026-10-07.

Notes to self / informal observations:
- Felt the heat on telemetry correlation: combine alert-minutes and quick links into a single slack context action button to speed manual overrides.
- Consider baking 'warm-kv-on-routing-change' as a default step in routing-control automation (cost vs benefit analysis required).

Attachments / snippets used in rehearsal:
- CLI commands run (copied to repo gists): gh:infra/gists/failover-commands-0915
- KV replay script version: kv-warmup v1.4 (sha: a3b2c1d)

Meeting rating (internal): useful rehearsal, several tactical fixes surfaced; recommend repeating quarterly or after infra changes that affect autoscaling or DNS behavior.

End of notes.
